title: Colour mixing chart
subject: Art & Design
unit: Summer 2: Sky painting and food (Splendid Skies and Chop, Slice & Mash)
source: Written for art/y1 lesson 10 (Colour mixing chart (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 10: Sky painting: tints and collage. Listen, look, then do the tasks with a grown-up.

blocks.answers: Red + yellow = orange; yellow + blue = green; red + blue = purple.

model.title: Make three blues for a sky

parts.text: Add a dot of blue and mix
Add more blue for the next one
Paint dark at the top, light near the ground

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Three blues from dark to light

panels.title: Add collage
points: Stick on clouds or a sunset

keywords.def: red, yellow or blue: colours we cannot mix
a colour made by mixing two primary colours
a colour made lighter by adding white
a picture made by sticking on paper pieces
how something looks or feels: rough, smooth, fluffy

questions.q: What do we add to make a tint?
Is green a primary or a secondary colour?
Core: Paint a sky with at least three tints of blue, darkest at the top.
questions.a: A sky painting with three tints from dark to light

questions.q: Extend: Add torn paper clouds or a sunset strip.
Stretch: Say which part of your sky you like best and why.
questions.a: For example: the orange sunset because the tints blend

questions.q: To make a lighter tint of blue, add:
questions.a: B) White. A tint is made by adding white. Black makes a darker shade.

questions.q: Big question: how many blues did you make?
questions.a: For example: three or more tints of blue by adding white
